high_consensus.description: This is a real operational gap for an opt-in primitive model. Without a defined disable/rollback path, stateful components (cron, ledgers, handoffs, audit chain) can be left inconsistent. High impact, relatively low documentation/design cost, and very actionable.

A normative JSON Schema for the shared audit envelope is foundational and prevents multi-sprint drift. Given every primitive extends CC-2 and schema-break risk is already identified as high, this has excellent ROI and clear acceptance criteria.

Hash-chain validation/recovery is essential for tamper-evident logging in production. The current gap is material: integrity checks without repair procedures create operational dead-ends. Domain-appropriate and strongly actionable.

This is a core security requirement, not a refinement. If operator identity and authorization are not concretely defined, handoff provenance and trust controls are unenforceable. Very high impact and should be explicitly specified.

blockers.concern: Audit log integrity requirements are incomplete for real tamper resistance (hash-chain only, no signing/identity guarantees).
blockers.why_matters: An attacker or faulty process can rewrite entire chains consistently if logs are writable; hash-chain alone proves structure, not author authenticity. This weakens auditor trust in critical events.
blockers.recommendation: Add signed envelopes (per-writer key), canonical serialization rules, and periodic external anchoring/checkpointing for high-assurance auditability.

blockers.concern: Configuration combinatorics are under-tested: operators may enable unsupported combinations despite only 5 tested tiers.
blockers.why_matters: The system explicitly allows arbitrary opt-in combinations, but behavior is only validated in selected tiers. Real-world operators will drift outside tested paths and encounter silent integration failures.
blockers.location: Supported Configuration Tiers; CC-9 degrade gracefully
blockers.recommendation: Enforce tier validation at startup (hard warning or block), or add compatibility matrix checks that refuse unsupported combinations unless an explicit override flag is set.

blockers.concern: Cost enforcement semantics are underspecified for day-boundary/timezone and multi-provider/multi-model billing lag.
blockers.why_matters: Ambiguity around 'daily cap' windows and delayed billing data can cause false halts or missed overruns, directly violating the fail-closed budget objective.
blockers.recommendation: Specify canonical budget window (UTC vs local), clock source, provider lag handling, and deterministic reconciliation rules across providers.

blockers.concern: Delivery plan is likely unrealistic: 7 P0 primitives + 9 cross-cutting requirements in 6-10 weeks with heavy review/audit gates.
blockers.why_matters: A slip in Sprint 1 cascades across all later sprints because shared infrastructure is front-loaded. This creates high probability of partial delivery, quality cuts, or unplanned de-scoping that undermines the cycle goals.
blockers.location: Timeline & Milestones; Scope & Prioritization; Risk R11
blockers.recommendation: Re-baseline now into two planned releases (core L1-L4 first, L5-L7 second), with explicit exit criteria per release and frozen scope per sprint.

blockers.concern: Sensitive data exposure risk in logs is not addressed despite storing full reasoning, handoff content, and identity text.
blockers.why_matters: JSONL logs may capture credentials, PII, proprietary context, or policy-sensitive prompts. Without redaction, ACLs, and encryption-at-rest guidance, this can create immediate security/compliance failures.
blockers.location: FR-L1-7, FR-L6, FR-L7, NFR-O4, Compliance section
blockers.recommendation: Add mandatory redaction pipeline, secret scanning on write, access controls, and retention/encryption requirements per log class.

blockers.concern: SessionStart surfaces untrusted text (handoffs/SOUL) without a clearly defined sanitization model for prompt-injection-safe rendering.
blockers.why_matters: If malicious or malformed content is surfaced into system context, it can steer agent behavior, leak secrets, or bypass intended prescriptive/descriptive boundaries.
blockers.recommendation: Define and implement strict SessionStart sanitization and delimiting rules, plus security tests for prompt injection in SOUL/handoff payloads.
